Community-driven time exchange platform connecting neighbors for mutual support

Designing a non-monetary economy requires solving complex trust and liquidity problems. How do you prevent inflation of 'time credits'? How do you ensure safety when strangers enter homes? How do you balance supply and demand in a hyper-local (5km) radius without a central market maker?

I architected a closed-loop economic model based on 'Time Credits' (1h = 60 credits). The core logic involves: 1) A progressive radius matching algorithm (expands search ring every 2 hours if unmatched). 2) A 'Family Pool' entity allowing cross-generation credit transfer (young earn, elderly spend). 3) A Trust Graph protocol requiring identity verification before 'Home Access' category requests are unlocked.
Economic Model: Self-regulating liquidity via cap-and-floor credit limits
Safety Architecture: Tiered access control based on user verification level
Scalability: Geo-sharded database design for hyper-local query performance
A time-banking platform that rebuilds community connections by enabling neighbors to exchange help using time as currency, creating sustainable mutual support networks in urban Thailand.

Gamified Health Data Platform & Cultural Exploration Engine

The Thai Health Promotion Foundation needed to drive physical activity data collection across 77 provinces. The challenge: How to make 'walking' addictive enough to generate consistent telemetry data without feeling like a chore?

I designed a 'Proof of Walk' protocol combining GPS telemetry with cultural checkpoints. The system architecture includes: 1) A 'Mission Engine' that dynamically generates quests based on geo-fences. 2) A flexible CMS allowing local municipalities to upload heritage content as 'Game Nodes'. 3) An anti-cheat algorithm verifying speed and route path consistency.
Architecture: Scalable 'Mission Engine' supporting 77 distinct provincial datasets
Engagement: 300% increase in daily active walking time vs baseline
Data: Structured telemetry pipeline ready for health policy analysis
